question.value: Is there a vibrationally excited H2O maser at 232.68670 GHz in Orion KL, blended with HCOOCH3, and where is it located?

evidence.quote: We investigated the ALMA science verification data of Orion KL and found a spectral signature of the vibrationally excited H$_{2}$O maser line at 232.68670 GHz

bands.value: Band 6 (215-245 GHz) SV spectral line survey; Cycle 0 band 6 continuum at 240-244 and 256-260 GHz

evidence.quote: They are part of a spectral line survey toward the Orion KL region at band 6 (215-245 GHz).

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: SV correlator resolution 488 kHz (0.60-0.65 km/s); Cycle 0 continuum resolution 15.625 MHz

evidence.quote: The spectral resolution of the ALMA correlator was 488 kHz, corresponding to the velocity resolution of 0.60$-$0.65 km s$^{-1}$ at the observed frequency range.

baselines.value: 17 to 265 kλ (22 to 345 m), 16 x 12 m antennas (SV)

evidence.quote: The baseline lengths ranged from 17 to 265 k$\lambda$ (from 22 to 345 m) consisted of 16$\times$12 m antennas.

angular_resolution.value: SV natural-weighted beam 1.7"x1.4", PA 171 deg; Cycle 0 uniform-weighted 0.74"x0.56", PA 101 deg

evidence.quote: The natural weighted beam size was 1$''$.7$\times$1$''$.4 with the position angle of 171$^{\circ}$.
The resultant typical rms (root-mean-square) noise level is 0.01$-$0.03 Jy beam$^{-1}$ for each channel map.
net on-source time for each setting was about 20 minutes

results_numeric.quantity: Compact Ridge integrated intensity, blended and pure

findings_qualitative.value: The 232 GHz H2O maser emission is concentrated at Source I and is unresolved at 1.7x1.4 arcsec resolution.

evidence.quote: the distribution of the 232 GHz H$_{2}$O maser features could not be resolved with the ALMA SV data

claims.hypothesis: The 232.68670 GHz vibrationally excited H2O maser is present in a YSO
claims.experiment: Compared blended and pure HCOOCH3 maps and spectra toward Source I
claims.result: Excess compact emission at Source I with double-peaked spectrum from -10 to 20 km/s
claims.finding: First detection of the 232 GHz vibrationally excited H2O maser in star-forming regions

evidence.quote: Therefore, we can safely conclude that at least the emission feature associated with Source I is the vibrationally excited H$_{2}$O maser line at 232.68670 GHz.

claims.hypothesis: The 232 GHz maser is related to the 22 GHz H2O or 43 GHz SiO masers
claims.result: Double peaks at similar velocities; closer to 22 GHz H2O masers
claims.finding: Likely associated with outflow/jet root or disk around Source I

evidence.quote: the 232 GHz maser features would have similar structure to that of the 22 GHz masers rather than the SiO masers

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Blending HCOOCH3 line and other lines (13CH3CH2CN, 13CH3CCH, acetone) considered; the Source I wide-velocity emission is not explained by them

evidence.quote: It is unlikely that other molecular lines with high velocity components contribute to this peak

limitations_admitted.value: Could not perfectly separate HCOOCH3 and H2O contributions due to insufficient spatial resolution

evidence.quote: we could not perfectly separate the contribution from the HCOOCH$_{3}$ and the 232 GHz H$_{2}$O maser lines mainly due to the insufficient spatial resolution

referee_caveats_inferred: Identification rests on the assumption that the pure HCOOCH3 line predicts the blended line's thermal emission
No LTE or non-LTE modelling to confirm maser nature
